The '''2024 NCAA Division I FBS football season''' was the 155th season of [[college football]] in the United States, the 119th season organized by the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] (NCAA), and the 49th of the highest level of competition, the [[NCAA Division I Football Bowl Subdivision|Football Bowl Subdivision]] (FBS). The regular season began on August 24 and ended on December 14. The postseason began on December 14, and, aside from any all-star games that were scheduled, ended on January 20, 2025, with the [[2025 College Football Playoff National Championship|College Football Playoff National Championship]] at [[Mercedes-Benz Stadium]] in [[Atlanta]]. This was the first season of the new [[College Football Playoff]] (CFP) system, with the bracket being expanded to 12 teams.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/35152132/rose-bowl-agrees-amended-deal-paving-way-early-cfp-expansion|title=Rose Bowl agrees to deal allowing early CFP expansion in '24|author=[[Pete Thamel|Thamel, Pete]]|website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=November 30, 2022|access-date=December 9, 2023}}</ref>

It was the first time since the [[2021 NCAA Division I FBS football season|2021 season]] that no major team finished the season undefeated, as the [[2024 Oregon Ducks football team|Oregon Ducks]], the season's last undefeated team, were defeated by the eventual national champion [[2024 Ohio State Buckeyes football team|Ohio State Buckeyes]] 41–21 in the [[2025 Rose Bowl|Rose Bowl]]. The season's [[Heisman Trophy]] winner was [[2024 Colorado Buffaloes football team|Colorado Buffaloes]] cornerback and wide receiver [[Travis Hunter]], the first [[two-way player]] to win the award since [[Charles Woodson]] in [[1997 NCAA Division I-A football season|1997]].

==Conference realignment==
{{main|2021–2026 NCAA conference realignment}}    
One school played its first FBS season in 2024. [[Kennesaw State Owls football|Kennesaw State]] (from [[NCAA Division I FCS independent schools|FCS independents]]) began its transition from [[NCAA Division I Football Championship Subdivision|Division I FCS]] in 2023 and joined [[Conference USA]] (CUSA) in July 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ksuowls.com/news/2022/10/14/general-kennesaw-state-to-join-conference-usa-in-2024-25.aspx|title=Kennesaw State to Join Conference USA in 2024-25|author=Alexander, Nolan|work=[[Kennesaw State Owls]]|date=October 14, 2022|access-date=December 9, 2023}}</ref> One formerly [[NCAA Division I FBS independent schools|independent]] school, [[Army Black Knights football|Army]], joined the [[American Conference (NCAA)|American Athletic Conference]] (AAC) in 2024.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.underdogdynasty.com/2023/10/26/23933036/army-black-knights-join-aac-2024-conference-move-american-athletic-conference-navy-game-realignment|title=Army will join the AAC in 2024: What to know about the Black Knights' conference move|author=Helwick, Steve|newspaper=[[SBNation]]|date=October 26, 2023|access-date=December 9, 2023}}</ref> [[SMU Mustangs football|SMU]] left the AAC and joined the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC) in 2024.<ref name="ACC" />

* [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]]: [[Arizona Wildcats football|Arizona]], [[Arizona State Sun Devils football|Arizona State]], [[Colorado Buffaloes football|Colorado]], and [[Utah Utes football|Utah]]<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/fannation/college/cfb-hq/ncaa-football/college-football-realignment-big-12-adds-3-schools-pac-12-responds|title=Big 12 votes to add Arizona, Arizona State, Utah in realignment move; Pac-12 responds|author1=Parks, James|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=August 4, 2023|access-date=December 9, 2023}}</ref>

The remaining two schools in the Pac-12, [[Oregon State Beavers football|Oregon State]] and [[Washington State Cougars football|Washington State]], made an agreement with the [[Mountain West Conference]] (MW) such that each remaining Pac-12 team will play six MW teams in 2024.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/39020713/oregon-state-washington-state-scheduling-agreement-mountain-west-faq|title=What Oregon State and Washington State's agreement with Mountain West means moving forward|author=Bonagura, Kyle|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=December 5, 2023|access-date=January 1, 2024}}</ref>

==Rule changes==
The following rule changes were approved by the NCAA Playing Rules Oversight Panel for the 2024 season:<ref>{{cite press release |url=https://www.ncaa.org/news/2024/3/1/media-center-football-rules-committee-proposes-technology-rules.aspx |title=Football Rules Committee Proposes Technology Rules |publisher=NCAA |date=March 1, 2024 |access-date=March 1, 2024}}</ref>
* Implementing a timeout at the first dead ball on or after the two-minute mark of the second and fourth quarters (similar to the NFL's [[two-minute warning]]). The following timing rules were synchronized to start after the two-minute timeout:
**Stopping the game clock when the offense gains a first down inbounds, then restarting after the chains are set.
**Situations where a 10-second runoff is required will now begin after the two-minute timeout instead of in the final minute of each half, mirroring an NFL rule change since [[2017 NFL season|2017]].
**If the defense commits an illegal substitution foul where 12 or more players participated in the down, in addition to the yardage penalty, the offense has the option to have the game clock reset to the time remaining before the snap. If the 12th player was in the process of leaving the field and not participating when the ball was snapped, the penalty enforcement will not include the clock reset option. This in-season change was a result of the Oregon Ducks using this tactic in the final 10 seconds of their game with the Ohio State Buckeyes on October 12.
* Allowing use of coach-to-player communications via the helmet for one player (indicated by a green dot on the helmet), which would be turned off either with 15 seconds on the play clock or when the ball is snapped, whichever occurs first.  
* The use of up to 18 tablets per team on the sidelines for in-game video only is now permitted.
* Team personnel (player/coach/assistant/etc.) who enter the field to engage officials with a tablet to review video of a play(s) are assessed an automatic unsportsmanlike conduct (15 yards) penalty which counts toward their limit of two before ejection.
* [[NCAA Division III|Division III]] adopted the first down timing rules that were implemented for FBS, FCS, and Division II in the [[2023 NCAA Division I FBS football season|2023 season]].
* Allowing conferences to use a collaborative instant replay system as a regular (instead of an experimental) rule.
* Horse-collar tackles within the tackle box are now penalized as a personal foul (15 yards).  Previously this action was not penalized within the tackle box.
* Head coaches are permitted to be interviewed by the media at the end of the first and third quarters, making permanent an experimental rule.
* Once the referee declares the first half ended, no replay reviews for that half are permitted.
* Commercial sponsor logos are permitted on three areas of the playing field.
* Any "hide-out" play, with or without a substitution, is considered a team unsportsmanlike conduct penalty (15 yards).
 
Points of emphasis for the 2024 season include:<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ncaapublications.com/p-4693-2024-ncaa-football-rules-book.aspx |title=2024 Official Football Rules |publisher=NCAA |date=June 18, 2024 |access-date=June 19, 2024}}</ref>
* Continued emphasis on targeting, taunting, concussions, feigning injuries, and low hits to the quarterback.
* Pre-snap actions (false start on offense, and disconcerting signals/causing the offense to false start) continue to be a point of emphasis, including editorial changes that if a defensive player is lined up within one yard of the line of scrimmage, he may not rush the line with the intent of causing a false start, and that any movement by the offense that simulates action will be a false start.
* Offensive alignment, including attention to eligible receivers being covered up by another player and other "gadget plays", will be strictly enforced.

== Headlines ==
* January 25, 2024 – The [[Mid-American Conference]] announced that it would eliminate its football divisions, effective immediately. The [[MAC Football Championship Game|championship game]] will instead involve the top two teams in the conference standings.<ref>{{cite press release |url=https://getsomemaction.com/news/2024/1/25/mac-announces-future-football-schedule-formats-for-2024-26.aspx |title=MAC Announces Future Football Schedule Formats for 2024-26 |publisher=Mid-American Conference |date=January 25, 2024 |access-date=February 27, 2024}}</ref>
* April 22 – The NCAA Division I Board of Directors announced the following:<ref>{{cite press release |url=https://www.ncaa.org/news/2024/4/22/media-center-division-i-board-of-directors-ratifies-transfer-nil-rule-changes.aspx |title=Division I Board of Directors ratifies transfer, NIL rule changes |publisher=NCAA |date=April 22, 2024 |access-date=April 23, 2024}}</ref>
** Effective immediately, all student-athletes who meet certain academic requirements will be immediately eligible when transferring to a new school, regardless of whether they had transferred before. Previously, all transfers after the first, except for graduate transfers, required that the student-athlete receive an NCAA waiver in order to be immediately eligible.
** Also effective immediately, schools will be allowed to directly assist their athletes in reaching [[Student athlete compensation|name, image, and likeness]] deals.
** After the end of the [[Pac-12 Conference]]'s operating year on August 1, the conference was officially removed from autonomy status, effectively turning the Power Five conferences into a Power Four.
* June 25 – The NCAA Division I Council announced the following:
** Effective immediately, all members of a team's staff can provide coaching services. While this effectively lifts most limits on the size of coaching staffs, it does not change limits on the number of coaches who can recruit off-campus, graduate assistants, or strength and conditioning coaches.<ref>{{cite press release |url=https://www.ncaa.org/news/2024/6/25/media-center-division-i-removes-some-restrictions-on-countable-coaches-in-football.aspx |title=Division I removes some restrictions on countable coaches in football |publisher=NCAA |date=June 25, 2024 |access-date=June 28, 2024}}</ref>
** Also effective immediately, cannabinoids were removed from the list of banned drugs in football. Penalties being served by student-athletes who had tested positive for cannabinoids were ended.<ref name="June25changes" />
** The Council voted to introduce a proposal that would reduce the duration of the [[NCAA transfer portal|transfer portal]] in football and basketball from 45 days to 30. A final vote was expected in October.<ref name="June25changes">{{cite press release |url=https://www.ncaa.org/news/2024/6/25/media-center-division-i-council-introduces-proposals-to-change-transfer-windows.aspx |title=Division I Council introduces proposals to change transfer windows |publisher=NCAA |date=June 25, 2024 |access-date=June 28, 2024}}</ref>
* August 27:<ref>{{cite press release |url=https://www.ncaa.org/news/2024/8/27/di-football-oversight-committees-propose-one-transfer-window.aspx |title=DI football oversight committees propose one transfer window |publisher=NCAA |date=August 27, 2024 |access-date=September 1, 2024}}</ref>
** The oversight committees for FBS and FCS recommended that the [[NCAA transfer portal|transfer portal]] be open only for a 30-day period, starting on the Monday after conference championship games. This will not affect the existing exceptions for participants in postseason games, which allows players to enter the portal within a 5-day window after their team's final game, or players undergoing a coaching change. The Division I Council voted on the change in October.
** Both oversight committees also approved a change to [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] rules. Effective immediately, the participation limit of four games for redshirting players no longer includes postseason games — conference championship games, bowls, FCS playoff games, and College Football Playoff games.
* October 9:<ref>{{cite press release |url=https://www.ncaa.org/news/2024/10/9/media-center-di-council-approves-changes-to-notification-of-transfer-windows-in-basketball-football.aspx |title=DI Council approves changes to notification-of-transfer windows in basketball, football |publisher=NCAA |date=October 9, 2024 |access-date=October 9, 2024}}</ref>
** The Division I Council approved the recommended reduction of the FBS and FCS transfer portal to 30 days, though with a different schedule than recommended. The fall window, which opens on the Monday after the FBS conference championship games, will be open only for 20 days. A 10-day spring portal will open in mid-April.
** The council also abolished the [[National Letter of Intent]] program effective immediately. Written offers of athletics aid will replace the NLI.

==Kickoff games==

This is the first year under the expanded College Football Playoff format. Under this format, the five highest-ranked conference champions will receive automatic bids, while the next seven highest-ranked teams will receive at-large bids. The four highest-ranked conference champions will receive a first-round bye in the playoff.<ref>{{Cite web |title=How the 12-team College Football Playoff will work: Teams, schedule, bids |url=https://www.ncaa.com/news/football/article/2024-02-20/how-12-team-college-football-playoff-will-work-teams-schedule-bids |access-date=2024-07-03 |website=www.ncaa.com |language=en}}</ref>{{#section-h:2024–25 College Football Playoff|Bracket}}

==Postseason==
{{main|2024–25 NCAA football bowl games}}

Normally, a team is required to have a .500 minimum [[winning percentage]] during the regular season to become [[bowl-eligible]] (six wins for an 11- or 12-game schedule, and seven wins for a 13-game schedule). If there are not enough winning teams to fulfill all open bowl slots, teams with losing records may be chosen to fill available bowl slots. Additionally, on the rare occasion in which a conference champion does not meet eligibility requirements, they are usually still chosen for bowl games via [[Bids to college bowl games|tie-ins]] for their conference.

==Television changes==
This was the first year of a new 10-year television deal for the [[Southeastern Conference]], whose games are now fully exclusive to ABC, [[SEC Network]] and the [[College Football on ESPN|ESPN networks]]. [[College Football on ABC|ABC]] replaces [[College Football on CBS Sports|CBS]] as the [[Terrestrial television|over-the-air]] television home of the SEC and exclusive television home of the [[SEC Championship Game]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportsmediawatch.com/news/sec-espn-deal-now-official-abc-replacing-cbs-will-go-into-effect-in-2024|title=SEC ESPN Deal Now Official ABC Replacing CBS Will Go Into Effect In 2024|website=SportsMediaWatch.com|date=December 10, 2020|accessdate=December 10, 2020}}</ref> 

[[Oregon State Beavers football|Oregon State]] and [[Washington State Cougars football|Washington State]], the two remaining members of the [[Pac-12 Conference]], announced a one-year agreement with [[CW Sports|The CW]] and [[Fox Sports (United States)|Fox]] (2 games) on May 14, 2024.<ref>{{cite news |date=May 14, 2024 |title=Pac-12 football to be featured nationally across The CW Network & FOX Sports in 2024|publisher=Pac-12|url=https://pac-12.com/news/2024/5/14/pac-12-football-be-featured-nationally-across-cw-network-fox-sports-2024.aspx |access-date=May 14, 2024}}</ref>

After extending their contract in March with the [[College Football Playoff]], ESPN sublicensed two first-round games to [[TNT Sports (United States)|TNT Sports]], their first since 2006. ESPN will also sublicense two quarterfinal bowl games to TNT beginning in 2026. The games were presented as an ESPN production, with no graphical changes or any hosts from TNT Sports.

Beginning this season, TNT Sports aired third-tier [[Mountain West Conference]] games on [[College Football on TNT Sports|TruTV]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lewis |first=Jon |date=2024-07-01 |title=TNT continues to add sports rights, picks up Mountain West |url=https://www.sportsmediawatch.com/2024/07/tnt-mountain-west-rights-deal-trutv-max-warner-bros-discovery/ |access-date=2024-07-02 |website=Sports Media Watch |language=en-US}}</ref>
